_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description:
The terminal renders with WebGL and falls back to the DOM on context loss. The test seeded a conversation at /c/term-webgl; terminals render with xterm.js, on a phone screen at device scale 1. window.__terminalCols lists the cols of every init and resize message the page's terminals sent their server, in order. "The WebGL canvas count" is the eval [...document.querySelector('.terminal-panel-content [data-terminal-id][style*="display: block"]').querySelectorAll("canvas")].filter(c => c.getContext("webgl2")).length.
1. Navigate to /c/term-webgl and open the Terminal workspace tool: phones keep workspace tools in the overflow menu, so click the visible button with aria-label exactly "More options", then the button in ".chat-overflow-popover" whose text starts with "Terminal".
2. The terminal, '.terminal-panel-content [data-terminal-id][style*="display: block"]', should become visible (wait up to 30s).
3. The WebGL renderer replaces the DOM renderer's rows with a canvas: the WebGL canvas count should become 1, and the terminal should contain no ".xterm-rows" (count 0).
4. The last entry of window.__terminalCols should become greater than 0. Record it in a window variable as the WebGL cols.
5. A context that is not restored (too many live contexts) must not leave the terminal blank. Eval: for every canvas in the terminal, c.getContext("webgl2")?.getExtension("WEBGL_lose_context")?.loseContext().
6. xterm waits briefly for a restore, then the DOM renderer takes over: the terminal's ".xterm-rows" should become visible (wait up to 10s) and contain "$". Then the WebGL canvas count must be 0 (check it once, right away).
7. The terminal refits to the DOM renderer's wider cells: the last entry of window.__terminalCols should become less than the WebGL cols.
